records.text: A world trigger that announces attacks on the Gates of the Blue Sapphire, Green Emerald, and Red Sun. Its alerts identify which gate is under attack.

High Overlord Saurfang leads the Horde assault toward Icecrown Citadel aboard Orgrim’s Hammer, directing the Kor’kron and champions to meet there. He asks whether Bolvar Fordragon survived, then commits to saving him and making the Lich King answer for his crimes. In the Battle for Undercity, he invokes counsel to Thrall and speaks of going home with an old friend.

The Lich King toys with his captives, telling Tirion Fordring that he engineered the champions’ path to Icecrown so they would fall into his hands. He sees their courage as a final surprise: they do not fear him, even as he claims power to remake the world in his image.

The Council of Six describes Lord Marrowgar as the Frozen Throne’s guardian, assembled by the Lich King from the bones of fallen adventurers. Marrowgar declares that none may enter his master’s sanctum and threatens to unleash the Scourge; his bone-themed attacks and taunts reinforce his role as a grim sentinel.

Festergut is a named Icecrown Citadel encounter creature whose brief, broken lines suggest a simple voice. He greets intruders with a playful “Fun time?”, vows to make them pay for killing Stinky, and later says he does not feel well.

Rotface is a named undead abomination in Icecrown Citadel's Abomination Wing. He greets combat with gleeful cries and talks about slime in childish, muddled phrases; when he dies, he cries out for “Precious.”

Professor Putricide is an experimental plague-maker in Icecrown Citadel's Abomination Wing. He announces disasters with cheery “Good news, everyone!” patter and boasts of a plague meant to destroy all life. He speaks of Rotface and Festergut with possessive fondness, valuing their remains as useful material.
Servants of the Throne are elite undead in the Abomination Wing of Icecrown Citadel. They use Glacial Blast in combat.
Nerub'ar Broodkeepers are elite undead in Icecrown Citadel's Abomination Wing, identified by their role tending a Nerub'ar brood.

Valithria Dreamwalker speaks as an individual combatant, calling for heroes to heal her wounds because she cannot hold off attackers much longer. As her strength returns, she urges them onward and says she has opened a portal into the Dream as their salvation. Her encounter lines also show her strain and loss of control as only nightmares remain, and her lament when a player dies.
Deathspeaker Servant is a Cult of the Damned combatant who casts Chaos Bolt.
Deathspeaker Disciple is a Cult of the Damned combatant who casts Shadow Bolt.
Deathspeaker Zealot is a Cult of the Damned combatant who casts Shadow Cleave.
Deathspeaker Attendant is a Cult of the Damned combatant who casts Shadow Bolt.
Deathspeaker High Priest is a Cult of the Damned combatant. It casts Aura of Darkness and Dark Reckoning.

Lady Deathwhisper praises her Master's limitless power and presents herself as one of the few able to see where true power lies. She demands whole, unquestioning devotion from those who serve and threatens destruction for those who oppose him. When resistance continues, she declares that she must take matters into her own hands.
The Decaying Colossus is a massive combatant whose recorded attack is Massive Stomp.
A Skybreaker Protector is a combatant with a defensive role. Its attack is Devastate.
A Skybreaker Vindicator is a combatant whose attack is Avenger's Shield.
A Skybreaker Dreadblade is a martial combatant whose attacks include Icy Touch and Plague Strike.

Deathbound Ward is an undead guardian of a master's sanctum. Its awakening lines react to the sanctum being disturbed and challenge whoever has arrived, giving it a wary, defensive presence. Its combat actions include Disrupting Shout and Saber Lash.
The Damned are undead combatants found in Icecrown Citadel. Their actions include Bone Flurry and Shattered Bones, reflecting their violent, skeletal character.
An ancient skeletal soldier is an undead fighter in Icecrown Citadel. Its combat action is Shield Bash, fitting a close-quarters role.
Puddle Stalker appears among the creatures in Icecrown Citadel.
Skybreaker Luminary is a humanoid encountered in Icecrown Citadel.
A Skybreaker Assassin is a humanoid combatant in Icecrown Citadel. Its attacks include Sinister Strike, matching the role implied by its name.
A Skybreaker Vicar is a humanoid assigned to the Icecrown Citadel area.
A Blighted Abomination is an abomination found in the Icecrown Citadel area. Its combat behavior includes Cleave.
A Plague Scientist is a plague-themed humanoid found in the Icecrown Citadel area. Its combat abilities include Combobulating Spray, Plague Blast, and Plague Stream.
Stinky is found in Icecrown Citadel.
A Skybreaker Sorcerer is a humanoid found in the Icecrown Citadel area. Its combat behavior includes casting Frostfire Bolt.
A Skybreaker Hierophant is a humanoid found in the Icecrown Citadel area.
A Kor'kron Stalker is a humanoid fighter whose combat style includes Sinister Strike.
A Kor'kron Primalist is one of the humanoid Kor'kron stationed in area 4812.
A Kor'kron Oracle is one of the humanoid Kor'kron stationed in area 4812.
A Kor'kron Defender is a humanoid fighter whose combat style includes Devastate.
A Kor'kron Invoker is a humanoid fighter who uses Frostfire Bolt in combat.
A Kor'kron Vanquisher is a humanoid fighter whose combat style includes Avenger's Shield.
A geist in Icecrown Citadel, the Vengeful Fleshreaper raises an alarm at the living’s arrival, calling for an ambush and warning that they cannot escape.
The Val'kyr Herald bears a herald's role in Icecrown Citadel.

Highlord Tirion Fordring leads the assault on Icecrown Citadel, rallying the heroes to fight with honor for their people’s freedom and safety. He urges them to master fear, invokes the Light, and declares his oath to kill Arthas and dismantle the Scourge—a vow he traces to Light's Hope. He also says the Light is sustaining Saurfang, whose soul is under great strain.

Highlord Darion Mograine speaks with solemn authority to those pursuing Shadow's Edge, warning that ambition can cost them their lives and souls. He takes personal responsibility for the path he sets them on, overseeing the weapon's forging and demanding souls and Shadowfrost Shards to unlock and seal its power. His words also honor the sacrifices made against the Lich King, while he invokes his father with devotion and grief.

Captain Arnath serves in the Argent Crusade and remembers fallen comrades as having lived and died in its service. His scripted exchanges reveal a dry, irritable edge: he complains about spoiled spider ichor and poor bat wings, and would rather die than spend another day gathering reagents for Finklestein. Other lines place his remarks amid death and resurrection.

Captain Brandon speaks as a wounded fighter who believes his injuries are beyond healing and urges his brothers to keep fighting. After being raised again, he describes the pain vanishing and calls others to join him in death; when he falls a second time, he apologizes. If the fight goes his way, he blesses those who have fought the Scourge and asks the Light to embrace them.

Captain Grondel fixates on fire even in death, asking that his remains be burned so he can be warm in the afterlife. Raised again, he turns that denied wish into a threat against everyone around him, taunting opponents about the burn. His final words show horror at what he has done, while a victory leaves him wondering what could redeem this unholy place.

Captain Rupert meets death with acceptance, calling the afterlife worthy. Raised again under the Lich King's will, he warns of an explosive encounter; his bomb jokes carry through the fight, and even his final warning asks others to stay in one piece. His words suggest a dry, danger-conscious sense of humor amid a battle he says he cannot escape.

Sister Svalna faces Crok as a former battle companion turned traitor in her eyes. She challenges him and Scourgebane in a contest to prove to their master who deserves the title of Champion, and scorns Crok's choice of ally. She treats the captains' deaths as unremarkable, but her own final words concede that Crok may have been right.

npcs.name: Crok Scourgebane

records.text: Crok Scourgebane is the Grand Champion of the Ebon Blade, fighting beside the Argent champions in Icecrown Citadel. He addresses them as brothers and urges them through the hall, calling the Vrykul defenders of the Frost Queen. Against Svalna, he offers to draw her attacks while the others return fallen brothers to their graves, then calls for a swift push before her reinforcements arrive.

npcs.title: Grand Champion of the Ebon Blade

records.text: A Ymirjar Battle-Maiden is a Vrykul combatant serving among the Frostwing forces at Icecrown Citadel. The battle-maiden title marks her role within the Ymirjar ranks.
A Ymirjar Warlord is a Vrykul combatant serving among the Frostwing forces at Icecrown Citadel. The warlord title marks a command role within the Ymirjar ranks.
A Ymirjar Huntress is a Vrykul combatant serving among the Frostwing forces at Icecrown Citadel. The huntress title marks her role as a hunter within the Ymirjar ranks.
A Skybreaker Marksman is a ranged fighter in the Skybreaker force at Icecrown Citadel, distinguished by a marksman's role in battle.

A Skybreaker Summoner is a spellcaster serving the Skybreaker force at Icecrown Citadel. Its combat actions include Curse of Doom, Incinerate and Shadow Bolt, giving this battlefield role a focus on damaging magic.

The Lich King claims dominion over Scourge ground and taunts a paladin that the Light cannot protect him there. He seeks a new champion, describes atrocities inflicted on a captive who still resists, and expects that captive and his challengers to serve him.
Highlord Bolvar Fordragon refuses the Lich King's attempt to make him serve. His emphatic “NEVER!” falters into a halting but repeated refusal: “I... I will never... serve... you...”

High Overlord Saurfang comes to claim the body of his son, Dranosh, who died at the Wrath Gate. He had promised Dranosh's mother to keep the boy safe, and promises a proper ceremony beside his mother's and ancestors' pyres in Nagrand. At Icecrown, he calls for the Lich King to answer for his crimes and for Bolvar to be saved.
A Kor’kron general.
Precious is a named creature in Icecrown Citadel. When roused, it gives a loud, baying howl.
Sindragosa's Ward is a defender who warns others to stop anyone approaching the Frost Queen.
An ambient frostwyrm found around Icecrown Citadel's spire.
A Frostwarden Handler, a humanoid associated with the frostwardens in Icecrown Citadel.
A Frostwing whelp found in Icecrown Citadel, one of a sizable group of its kind.
Rimefang is a named creature in Icecrown Citadel.
Spinestalker is an undead creature.
A Spire Gargoyle is an undead gargoyle.
A Spire Minion is an undead minion.
A Frenzied Abomination is an undead abomination.
A Darkfallen Advisor is an undead advisor.
Fury is an undead creature.

Stefan Vadu faces the Lich King's presence firsthand: he says the enemy's voice taunts him and calls for the two of them to silence the Lich King. His words show personal resolve in the confrontation.
A Darkfallen Blood Knight of the San'layn, one of the named San'layn combat ranks found in Icecrown.
A Darkfallen Commander of the San'layn, a named command rank among their forces in Icecrown. Its battle shout marks a battlefield role.
A Darkfallen Noble of the San'layn, identified by noble rank among their forces in Icecrown.
A Darkfallen Archmage of the San'layn, a named magical rank among their forces in Icecrown.
A Darkfallen Lieutenant of the San'layn, a named officer rank among their forces in Icecrown. Its Vampiric Curse marks a combat capability.
A Darkfallen Tactician, identified as one of the San'layn.
Alchemist Finklestein is an Ashen Verdict quartermaster who offers goods and repair services.
Crusader Grimtong is a warrior armor crafter and seller, identified by that role in his greeting and title.
Commander Kunz is a humanoid commander at Icecrown Citadel.
Crusader Halford is a paladin armor crafter and seller, identified by that role in his greeting and title.
A fixed trap in Icecrown Citadel.
A flesh-eating insect found in Icecrown Citadel.

Deathbringer Saurfang is an undead Scourge champion who invokes the Lich King. He calls an old orc his father, urges him to join the Scourge's conquest, and boasts of surpassing his strength. He summons heroes to face the Scourge and speaks of the fallen being raised into its armies.
An Abomination Wing Mad Scientist Stalker in Icecrown Citadel.
A Kor'kron reaver serving in the Saurfang event at Icecrown Citadel, one of the combat roles associated with that encounter.
An Argent Champion appearing in the Icecrown Citadel conflict, identified by a title that marks a champion's role.
Valithria Dreamwalker is a named dragonkin encountered in Icecrown Citadel.

Blood-Queen Lana'thel is a vampiric queen whose battle speech centers on hunger and blood: she demands that foes know her hunger, claims a bitten victim as hers, and taunts opponents with cool confidence. Even in defeat, she sounds almost regretful that the fight has ended.

Prince Valanar is a Darkfallen prince who boasts of the orb’s power and vows vengeance over Naxxanar. When the Invocation of Blood selects him, he announces his turn with grand confidence; he relishes serving dinner and demonstrating Darkfallen power.

Prince Keleseth boasts that the Darkfallen Orb makes him invincible and threatens that blood will flow. He addresses his queen in his final words, revealing allegiance, while his kill lines sneer at opponents and invoke death as truth.
Prince Taldaram is a named combatant whose invocation claims power from an orb. He delights in pain and taunts mortals, threatening them with death and demanding that they beg for mercy.
Ikfirus the Vile is a named rogue armor vendor. His greeting describes crafting and selling Shadowblade armor for rogues.
Tortunok is a named druid armor vendor. His greeting describes crafting and selling Freya's Lasherweave armor for druids.
Gerardo the Suave is a named hunter armor vendor. His greeting describes crafting and selling Ahn'kahar Blood Hunter armor for hunters.
A humanoid Ebon Champion in Icecrown Citadel.
Blood-Queen Lana'thel leads the San'layn, calling them the Lich King's immortal soldiers. She rallies her brothers against their enemies and mocks mortals who think they have defeated them.
Scott the Merciful is identified with Priest Armor and presents himself as an artisan who crafts and sells Crimson Acolyte armor for priests.
Ymirjar Deathbringers are Frostwing vrykul combatants, identified by their deathbringer role.

The Lich King is portrayed ordering his forces to destroy the green dragon and leave her for reanimation. Darion Mograine's Shadowmourne quest frames the Lich King as the target of vengeance for his campaign and the heroes lost to it.
Haragg the Unseen is a warlock armor crafter associated with Dark Coven armor made for warlocks.
Torgo the Elder is a humanoid in Icecrown Citadel.
The Plagued Insect is an insect critter.
The Frozen Insect is an insect critter.
The Blood Parasite is a parasite critter.
The Blood Spider is a spider critter.
Uvlus Banefire is a mage armorer associated with Bloodmage armor, which he says he crafts and sells for magi.
An invisible, non-interactive stalker helper.

Ormus the Penitent recalls being a paladin and says he committed sins as one of the Lich King's Death Knights. He seeks atonement by making powerful rings for allies fighting the Scourge. He says the Light shuns him, but he will aid his allies and refuses to wield dark powers. He also offers Death Knight armor.
A non-interactive stalker helper named for tear-gas targeting.
A Nightmare Cloud encounter helper associated with Valithria.

Infiltrator Minchar is an Argent Crusade quest contact at Icecrown Citadel. He asks for help recovering Darnavan, a former ally whose Cult of the Damned brainwashing has made him a threat; Minchar welcomes Darnavan's return and values the intelligence he brings from inside the Citadel.

A Scourge giant on Icecrown Citadel's Ramparts, this behemoth hurls debris at approaching vessels and keeps smaller ships from landing safely. The Kor'kron and Skybreaker forces each identify it as an obstacle to clearing a safe landing. It is infected with the Death Plague.

A Kor'kron officer at Icecrown Citadel, this Horde lieutenant directs help against the Rotting Frost Giant, which is holding up a safe landing on the Ramparts. He celebrates the giant's defeat for the Horde and looks ahead to drinking together once the Frozen Throne has been destroyed.

A Skybreaker officer assigned to Icecrown Citadel's Ramparts, this Alliance lieutenant seeks help clearing a safe landing for the fleet. The Rotting Frost Giant's attacks on nearby vessels are keeping smaller ships at bay; the lieutenant celebrates its defeat and anticipates the advance toward the Frozen Throne.
A rotting frost giant, this hulking Scourge-side threat hurls debris at nearby ships and blocks a safe landing at the Ramparts. It is reported infected with the Death Plague.

Alchemist Adrianna is an alchemist who came to the front lines to oversee efforts to obtain live Scourge blight samples after agents repeatedly failed. Her research aims to help develop an antidote, and she is prepared to study infected living hosts by harvesting samples from them.

Alrin the Agile is one of his side’s best agents, sent to watch the San’layn. While investigating a resurrection ritual in the Crimson Halls, he was caught and held for interrogation; he says he does not know Tirion’s plans of attack.

Infiltrator Minchar is a named agent captured by the San’layn while investigating a resurrection ritual in the Crimson Halls. He is held and interrogated there, and his cries can be heard through the halls.

Valithria Dreamwalker is a dragon who has endured the dark magics of Icecrown. She shares the Life Crystal secret she used to resist them, drawing on the verdant Dragonshrine in Dragonblight. Against Sindragosa, she asks companions to use the crystals to draw out Sindragosa’s essence before defeating her.

Jaina Proudmoore is deeply affected by Arthas’s fate. The locket tells her he kept it, and she senses that part of him remained alive, trapped and struggling. She wonders whether he might someday remember who he was and hopes he can find rest beyond the icy grip of Frostmourne.

Muradin Bronzebeard remembers Arthas as his brother and the lad he trained in Lordaeron. The blade brings back memories of sharpening Arthas’s skills and preparing him for a great destiny. Muradin treasures that moment from their past and bids Arthas farewell with grief.

Uther is a spirit still burdened by anxiety and dark thoughts that distance him from the Light. He has long struggled to forgive Arthas for his transgressions, yet keeps the memory of presenting him with a medal close to his heart. After receiving that memory, Uther says his soul may finally rest.

Sylvanas sees the Lich King's defeat as vengeance for the atrocities inflicted on her people, while remembering the terrible cost of their weakness and pride. Having been deceived by the Lich King before, she had scarcely trusted her senses when he fell. Her thoughts then turn to those freed from his grasp who remain bound to mortal life.
Vol'guk is a shaman armorer who says he crafts and sells Frost Witch armor for shamans. His greeting identifies his trade.
Goodman the “Closer” is an Emblem of Frost quartermaster in Icecrown Citadel. He offers goods and repair services.
Putricide’s Trap is a scripted trap associated with Putricide in Icecrown Citadel.
Wicked Spirit is an elite undead presence in Icecrown Citadel, one of several of its kind found there.
Garrosh Hellscream is Overlord of the Warsong Offensive. He frames the Horde’s campaign in Icecrown Citadel as close to victory and sees the Lich King’s death as a source of glory for the Horde.
Aronen is an apprentice to Ormus who serves as a quest contact in Icecrown.
